hannah: Heads up we're seeing a sharp spike in webinar signups at 05:42 UTC, up ~4x vs baseline. Can someone check attribution before the 09:00 KPI review?
diego: Looking now. Which segment/landing?
hannah: Webinar -> Product Intro landing.
rachel: Pulling GA and SFDC. Quick check: GA shows referrals from partner-c, but utm_campaign values alternate between `q2_webinar` and `q2-webinar-ptc`.
diego: That will split our campaign counts. Ops, any sends around 05:40? @ops-bot
ops-bot: Event: scheduled-send-982 executed at 2026-05-18T05:39:50Z recipients=2,600 template=partner-cohort-c. Links tracked.
analytics-bot: SFDC excerpt: 
```
nlead_id,created_at,utm_campaign,assigned_queue
L-12001,2026-05-18T05:42:03Z,q2_webinar,SDR-EMEA
L-12002,2026-05-18T05:42:45Z,q2-webinar-ptc,SDR-EMEA
L-12003,2026-05-18T05:43:12Z,q2_webinar,SDR-NA
```
rachel: Routing looks fine. Main issue is attribution fragmentation. Suggest we add `campaign_canonical` in ETL mapping both campaign variants -> `q2_webinar` for reporting. Don't overwrite original utm fields.
diego: Agree. For the KPI slide, show raw vs canonical counts and a footnote: "partner send at 05:39 caused one-off lift; counts normalized for trend."
hannah: Also add mini-quality check: MQL% for this spike vs 7-day baseline. If quality lower, mark as low-confidence.
ops-bot: Action: create mapping rule `canonicalize_q2_webinar` in ETL. ETA 1h. Webhook: https://hooks.redwood.internal/marketing/normalizers
analytics-bot: Dashboard annotation added: "partner send detected: scheduled-send-982 (05:39 UTC)"
rachel: I'll build two tiny panels: raw signups, canonical signups, and MQL comparison. Will add footnote and hide spike from trendline smoothing.
hannah: Perfect. Quick sync 08:50 to finalize slide before the KPI call. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
